qa_pair.question: An approach to limiting request volume was considered and turned down, and a later entry replaced that reasoning entirely. In the entry that replaced it, how many simultaneous callers were used to demonstrate the replacement behaved correctly?
Exactly one source file in the store is referenced by entries of three different categories. What is the path of that file?

Two entries describe checks that reported a clean result while actually verifying nothing. One was caused by the way a command-line tool aligns its output. In the other, traffic left the machine from more than one address; when the volume was raised high enough to reach the ceiling, how many of those requests were turned away?
One entry explains why a table-level guard intended to require at least one array element never refused anything. Which migration file does that entry point to?
Counting every scope recorded in the store, how many entries belong to something other than the school management system codebase?
How many entries in the store are categorised as a production failure rather than as a choice, a durable statement, a working preference, or an abandoned approach?
Among the entries marked as describing something that broke and was later corrected, one concerns a component that rendered dates. What file does that entry name?
A shared wrapper component caused one control to activate another when a group of them was placed inside it. Which file containing that wrapper is named in the entry describing the problem?

The store records a case where published guidance from an outside provider was deliberately not followed, because obeying it would have allowed a weaker check to be substituted for a stronger one. Which handler file do both that entry and the related failure report name?
Ignoring entries that have been replaced by a newer one, how many entries does the store hold in total?
